findings.title: T13's result-discovery premise is false and its fallback cannot satisfy the offer contract
findings.description: T13 instructs: "reuse 320's existing result-discovery surface rather than re-implementing a review-file scan; if no such surface exists yet, scope this task to the store-recorded samples only and note the gap rather than inventing a new file-walk." I verified no such surface exists: `capture.resolve_target` (src/squadron/metrology/capture.py:64-121) resolves a single caller-named target (a per-index glob, not an enumeration); `MetrologyStore` globs only its own record directory (store.py:174); `report.enrich_samples` reads only files already referenced by samples. Worse, the named fallback is logically impossible for the function's purpose: `select_residual_offers` must find results **not yet sampled** (T13's own bullet: "no `SampleVerdict.result_ref` points at them"), but store-recorded samples are by definition the **sampled** ones — the exact complement. Under the fallback the function can never return a non-empty offer set, contradicting T13's own success criteria ("3 unsampled matching results at `rate=1.0` yields 3 `OfferTarget`s"), T14's tests (non-empty guarantee, exhausted, `rate=0.5` over 4 unsampled results, pruned file at lines 215-219), and the asserted success criterion "a graduated config with unsampled results yields a non-empty offer set" — an explicit architecture commitment. The lapse-detection bullet (line 203) and the pruned-file test also require enumerating current review files. Fix before execution: add an explicit result-discovery step — enumerate `project-documents/user/reviews/*-review.*` under cwd, derive each file's `JudgeConfigId` via 320's `derive_judge_config_id`, subtract sampled `result_ref`s — as a small standalone task or an explicit T13 bullet, replacing the impossible fallback (this also removes the need for the mid-task "ask the Project Manager" stall).

findings.title: T3's placement of GraduatedConfig creates a circular import with T11's envelope extension
findings.description: T3 defines `GraduatedConfig` in `calibration_models.py` with `judge_config: JudgeConfigId` (line 64), and `JudgeConfigId` lives in `src/squadron/metrology/models.py` — so `calibration_models` must import from `models`. T11 then extends `MetrologyRecord` in `models.py` (line 175) with `graduated_config: GraduatedConfig | None`, forcing the reverse import. Both load orders fail: whichever module is imported first leaves the other partially initialized and its needed name undefined. 321's `report_models.py` has the same one-way shape but no back-edge, which is why it works. A junior AI cannot complete T11 as written without deviating from T3's explicit placement. Fix: define `GraduatedConfig` in `models.py` — it is a store payload, matching that module's own docstring ("shapes persisted to and read from the metrology store", models.py:1-3) and the `SampleVerdict` precedent next to the envelope (models.py:100-111) — and keep the recommendation/offer models in `calibration_models.py`.

findings.title: T7's numbered precedence contradicts its own clarification and T8's required test
findings.description: T7 says to implement the bands "in this precedence order" with case 1 (`n < floor` → `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`) evaluated first, then case 4 (`TIGHTEN`) carrying the parenthetical that a below-floor low-match cell "still surfaces as `TIGHTEN`, not `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`" (line 119). As literally ordered, case 1 fires first for every below-floor cell, so case 4 is unreachable for exactly the cells the clarification (line 121) and T8's test (line 134: "`n < floor` with a low match rate returns `TIGHTEN`, not `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`") require. A junior AI following the numbered order produces code that fails T8. The intent is recoverable — the clarification and the test agree with each other — but the spec must be corrected so `match_rate <= tighten_rate` is checked *before* the floor/unversioned gates, and while doing so it should pin the one interaction neither the design's table nor T7 resolves: an **unversioned** cell with a low match rate (`TIGHTEN` or `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`?).

findings.title: Malformed-judge-block failure mode is claimed covered but absent from T7/T8
findings.description: The coverage check asserts "malformed judge block (inherited from `resolve_thresholds`, exercised in T8)" — but T8 (lines 129-140) contains no malformed-block test, and T7's `read_current_thresholds` (line 122) specifies handling only for unregistered templates. The design's Failure Modes row requires an explicit handling decision, a WARNING naming the template, and a test ("malformed judge block → flagged, not silently defaulted"). The handling also needs a decision the design leaves open: `resolve_thresholds` (src/squadron/pipeline/actions/judge.py:49-55) does `float(pass_floor)` and raises `ValueError` on a non-numeric floor — it does not "fall back" — so T7 must catch and flag (e.g., `current=None` + WARNING) rather than inherit silently. Add the branch to T7 and the test to T8, or strike the row from the claimed coverage.

findings.title: model_dimension_note spec drops the runtime-drawn-model clause the success criterion requires
findings.description: The success criterion requires "the runtime-drawn-model limitation is stated where the recommendation is produced", and the design spells it out: where a step draws its model at runtime (a 180 pool), the note states the threshold cannot track the drawn model and the recommendation does not apply to that step. T9's note-text bullet carries only the (template, model)-pairing clause, and T10 asserts only non-emptiness — so a note omitting the runtime-pool clause passes every test in this breakdown and the criterion's second half ships silently unmet. Add the clause to T9's bullet (and optionally a content assertion to T10).

findings.title: offers --project has no implementable semantics under the specified data model
findings.description: Both the design's API contract and T15 give `sq metrology offers [--project ID] ...`, but `GraduatedConfig` (line 64) carries no project dimension — only `judge_config`, `artifact_level`, `evidence`, `graduated_at`. Samples carry `ProjectId` (that is how `recommend --project` filters via `store.list_samples`), but graduations do not, so there is nothing for the flag to filter on; ignoring it would be a silent no-op, which this slice's own discipline forbids. Either drop `--project` from `offers` or define it (e.g., record the project on the graduation, or filter offer targets by the cwd-derived project via 320's `derive_project_id`). Worth pinning at the same time: `graduate` has no `--project` flag yet must "re-derive via the same path as `recommend`", which needs a sample-listing scope — presumably the cwd-derived project, but T15 does not say.
